goal: Repository operators can manually trigger a real pipeline and administer the existing repository settings surfaces through a dense, responsive information hierarchy without invented metadata, mutations, or server capabilities.
non_goals: Do not edit backend, API endpoint/type, router, RepoWrapper, repository store, authentication, permission calculations, shared organization/admin/user secret or registry behavior, dependencies, or approved prototype files.

Do not add repository name/description editing, secret audit/usage data, registry verification, cron last-result data, badge visual styles, cache cleanup, export, archive, or extension marketplace semantics.
Do not close baseline tasks 4.4 or 4.5 from this implementation slice.
expected_evidence: Focused component, route, and pure-function tests proving manual-run loading/validation/submission, admin navigation, supported settings rendering, inherited-resource boundaries, cron actions, badge formatting, destructive pending state, and extension submission.
Full frontend Vitest plus targeted Prettier, ESLint, TypeScript, Vite build, and git diff receipts.
Current desktop and 390px browser evidence for manual-run, general settings, resource table, badge, and danger-region states without page-level horizontal overflow.
Evidence-bearing task report plus independent spec and quality reviews for baseline task 4.3.
unsafe_assumptions: Prototype-only metadata and actions are unsupported and must not be inferred from current entities.
Branch APIs expose names only, and extension fields represent endpoint configuration rather than installable cards.
Inherited secrets and registries remain read-only, and operational success exists only after the current API resolves.
stop_condition: Stop if implementation needs a new field, endpoint, mutation, route, store contract, permission rule, backend behavior, prototype fixture, or edit outside the locked task files.
